title: An Exploratory Evaluation of LLM-Assisted Rewriting of Moderate-Complexity Financial Sentences for DisCoCat-Based Sentiment Analysis
abstract: Quantum natural language processing (QNLP) provides a grammar-aware framework for text modeling, and Distributional Compositional Categorical (DisCoCat) is one of its theoretically grounded formulations. Prior work on financial sentiment analysis has identified practical limitations of DisCoCat, including parser sensitivity, high simulation cost, and difficulty handling longer sentences. We study an LLM-assisted preprocessing workflow that uses controlled rewriting to compress, simplify, or decompose moderate-complexity financial sentiment sentences into parser-compatible, circuit-efficient variants while preserving sentiment-bearing meaning. We compare prompting strategies, language models, and filtering configurations with the low-complexity-only DisCoCat baseline of Stein et al. At the circuit level, the strongest compression variants reduce average qubit and gate counts by more than 70 percent relative to the raw moderate-complexity subset. Across repeated training runs, GPT-4.1-mini with Prompt B achieves the highest observed mean accuracy, $0.550 \pm 0.035$, compared with $0.521 \pm 0.050$ for the baseline. Larger training splits do not necessarily improve downstream performance; across evaluated configurations, training-split size has a moderately negative association with accuracy (Pearson $r=-0.446$). These results provide exploratory evidence that LLM-assisted rewriting can make some moderate-complexity inputs usable within the evaluated DisCoCat configuration, while highlighting prompt design, filtering, and circuit-aware preprocessing as considerations for more scalable QNLP-based financial sentiment analysis.
summary: This paper proposes using Large Language Models (LLMs) to rewrite complex financial sentences into simplified forms suitable for DisCoCat-based sentiment analysis within a Quantum NLP framework. The method successfully reduces the computational complexity of the resulting quantum circuits while maintaining high classification accuracy, demonstrating a potential pathway for applying quantum models to real-world language tasks.
main_problem: The paper addresses practical limitations of using DisCoCat for financial sentiment analysis when processing complex, long sentences due to issues like parser sensitivity and high computational cost.
main_result: LLM-assisted rewriting successfully compresses moderate-complexity inputs into circuit-efficient variants, achieving higher mean accuracy (0.550) than the low-complexity baseline using GPT-4.1-mini with Prompt B.
method: A novel preprocessing workflow is proposed where Large Language Models (LLMs) are used to rewrite and simplify complex financial sentences into forms compatible with the DisCoCat framework, which maps grammar to quantum circuits.
model_or_system: The core model is Quantum Natural Language Processing (QNLP) utilizing Distributional Compositional Categorical (DisCoCat). The computational object derived from the text structure is a parameterized quantum circuit.
key_observables: Mean classification accuracy, average qubit and gate counts on the resulting quantum circuits, and linguistic complexity metrics.
important_parameters: Prompting strategies (e.g., Prompt B), specific LLMs (GPT-4.1-mini), and filtering configurations are key parameters being compared.
main_assumptions: The study assumes that controlled rewriting can preserve the sentiment-bearing meaning of the original complex text while reducing computational overhead for quantum circuit mapping.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the pipeline, showing how a parser-derived diagram (Figure 1) from a sentence like 'Amazon profits soar' is reduced and mapped to a parameterized ansatz quantum circuit (Figure 2).
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem limitations of DisCoCat for complex text, details the LLM-assisted rewriting workflow involving multiple prompting strategies, presents quantitative comparisons against a low-complexity baseline, and concludes with an assessment of the feasibility.
why_interesting: While not focused on core quantum hardware physics, the work explores using advanced AI (LLMs) to preprocess inputs for quantum algorithms, which is relevant for developing practical applications in quantum machine learning.
